rules: Signal on day t, bought at the next open. Returns before costs; after_costs takes off 0.49% a round trip. index_pct and lead_pct are against the Nifty 500 over the sessions each pick was held.
choice_rule: For each list the version taken is the best on 2017-2021 (lead over the index for lists 1, 2 and 4; share of picks that rose, among versions still profitable after costs, for list 3). Its 2022-2026 record is printed whatever it is.

box_20_tight.what: Twenty sessions inside a 12% range, then a close above it on twice the usual volume, finishing in the top 30% of the day's range. Above the 200-day average.

box_40.what: Forty sessions inside an 18% range, then a close above it on twice the usual volume. Above the 200-day average.

box_60.what: Sixty sessions inside a 25% range, then a close above it on twice the usual volume. Above the 200-day average.

box_40_any_trend.what: The forty-session box, whatever the longer trend.

box_40_lighter_volume.what: The forty-session box on one and a half times the usual volume.

box_40_leader.what: The forty-session box, only in stocks whose leader score is in the top half.

box_40_tightest.what: A close above a forty-session range that was among the tightest 30% on the exchange that day, on one and a half times the usual volume.

ema20_pullback.what: An uptrend that dipped to its 20-day average in the last three sessions and closed back above it, above the previous day's high.

golden_cross.what: The 50-day average crossed above the 200-day in the last five sessions.

ema_20_50_cross.what: The 20-day average crossed above the 50-day in the last five sessions, above the 200-day average.

stack_and_strength.what: Price above its 20-, 50- and 200-day averages in order, RSI between 55 and 70, MACD above its signal line and rising, ADX at 25 or more.

scorecard.what: Nine textbook conditions (above the 20-, 50- and 200-day averages in order, RSI over 55, MACD above its signal line, ADX at 25 with +DI ahead, more volume on up days, volume above its usual, within 5% of the 52-week high). The fifteen stocks meeting the most, seven at least, every five sessions.

rsi2_under_10.what: In an uptrend, with the two-day RSI under 10: sold off hard for a day or two.

rsi2_under_10_leader.what: The same, only in market leaders (top 30%).

rsi2_under_5.what: In an uptrend, with the two-day RSI under 5.

three_down_days.what: In an uptrend, three lower closes in a row.

below_lower_band.what: In an uptrend, a close under the lower Bollinger band (20 days, 2 deviations).

gap_down_recovered.what: Above its 200-day average, opened 2% or more under the previous close and closed above its open.

the_week_list.what: The existing week list (a leader that fell this week), for comparison.

money_flow.what: The four sectors where money is moving in (share of market turnover this week against its own sixty-session share, share of members above their 50-day average, and the month's median move), and the four strongest leaders in each.

turnover_share_only.what: The four sectors whose share of market turnover rose most this week, and the four strongest leaders in each.

sector_momentum.what: The four sectors with the best median three-month move, and the four strongest leaders in each.

emerging_leaders.what: Leader score under the 45th percentile a month ago and over the 60th now. Ranked on how far it rose.

stock_turnover_surge.what: Turnover this week at twice its sixty-session usual or more, the week up, in an uptrend. Ranked on the surge.

breakout.exit: 21 sessions, or a close 8% under the entry
breakout.note: The version was chosen as the rule says, on leaving at a close back under the base. Both exits were measured for every version. Leaving at the base cut the average and left three picks in ten ahead; a line 8% under the entry left five in ten ahead with a higher average. The site uses the second. That choice between the two exits was made after seeing both.

quick.exit: the same, or a close 7% under
quick.note: The rule chose among versions still profitable after costs on 2017-2021, and only a plain five-session hold was (52 picks in 100 rose). The reader asked for the highest share of picks rising, so the site runs the exit with the highest: sold on the first close above the 5-day average. Its average pick does NOT cover a 0.49% round trip, and the page says so beside it.
